sections.heading: Ooma limitation, pricing interpretation, and alternative context
sections.body:
Limitation: SMS allotments are account-wide caps (e.g. Pro ~250/mo) — not per-user unlimited; Call queues, CRM and auto-dialer require Pro Plus; Roughly 15-seat cliff — larger teams often outgrow Office into Enterprise or peers because it forces process changes or add-ons around Ooma when cloud phone is the job.

Pricing interpretation: no free plan confirmed — scope a paid pilot on Essentials with exit criteria before annual seats.

Plan trade-off: you gain call recording (Essentials, Pro, Pro Plus) at the expense of Entry price and seat minimums vs routing, CTI and analytics depth — measure both in the pilot. Researched packaging: Essentials · cloud phone | Pro | Pro Plus.

Alternative context: unlike CallHippo, Ooma is preferable when Small businesses that want transparent monthly VoIP without annual contracts because cloud phone plus call recording (Essentials, Pro, Pro Plus) match; prefer CallHippo when Contact-centre / multi-skill agent operations (prefer Talkdesk/Genesys/Five9) because the operating loops differ.

sections.heading: Decision scenario and conclusion for Ooma
sections.body:
Scenario: recommend Ooma for Small businesses that want transparent monthly VoIP without annual contracts; do not choose it when Contact-centre / multi-skill agent operations (prefer Talkdesk/Genesys/Five9) — the jobs diverge at call recording (Essentials, Pro, Pro Plus).

Implementation time: weeks to configure cloud phone if Salesforce, HubSpot, Google Workspace, Microsoft Teams must be green before invites.

Integrations in research: Salesforce, HubSpot, Google Workspace, Microsoft Teams.

Decision conclusion: buy Ooma when researched fit (Small businesses that want transparent monthly VoIP without annual contracts) beats researched limits (SMS allotments are account-wide caps (e.g. Pro ~250/mo) — not per-user unlimited); otherwise keep researching — do not substitute product names into a generic setup essay.
